executed.title: Axis-order swap trap (Web Mercator arithmetic)
executed.code_summary: Pure-stdlib EPSG:3857 forward/inverse (R=6378137) + haversine; round-trips (lon 13.405, lat 52.520); then feeds the same two values with latitude in the longitude slot; reports resulting position and great-circle displacement from the intended point.
executed.expected: Correct order round-trips exactly; swapped order yields a valid-looking but wrong coordinate pair thousands of km away (no exception raised).
executed.scope_limits: Arithmetic-only demonstration of the axis-order failure class (proposal §3, §5.2); does not exercise PROJ/GDAL or any Fieldbook code; spherical Web Mercator formulas, not library transforms; sandbox resource limits above apply.

executed.expected: R*Tree available; plan uses the virtual-table index; indexed query much faster than full scan; identical hit counts (no rows lost).

executed.title: Three-way field merge semantics (toy function)
executed.code_summary: Per-field 3-way merge(base, mine, theirs): identical edits collapse; disjoint edits auto-merge; same-field divergence and delete-vs-edit produce conflict records carrying base/mine/theirs values.
executed.expected: Case1 disjoint edits merge with empty conflict list; Case2 note edited on both sides -> conflict {base:'birch', mine:'v1 text', theirs:'v2 text'}; Case3 theirs deleted note while mine edited -> conflict with theirs:null.

observed_stdout.case1_disjoint_edits: merged {lat:52.521, lon:13.4, name:'Plot A (renamed)', note:'birch, moss'}, conflicts []
observed_stdout.case2_same_field_edited_both: merged keeps base for untouched fields, conflicts [{field:'note', base:'birch', mine:'v1 text', theirs:'v2 text'}]

executed.scope_limits: 20-line reference function on flat JSON fields; demonstrates the conflict-surfacing semantics chosen in §6.2, not the product merger (no revision chains, no geometry, no identifier map).

executed.title: Commit boundary: uncommitted work invisible and discarded on crash-like close (component check)
executed.code_summary: File-backed SQLite DB in WAL mode; connection A commits row 1, opens a transaction, inserts row 2 without committing; connection B counts rows; A closes without commit (crash-like); fresh connection re-counts.
executed.expected: journal_mode=wal; B sees 1 row while the transaction is open; after crash-like close only the committed row remains.
executed.scope_limits: Consistency sample for SQLite's documented atomic-commit guarantee [S9]; does not test Fieldbook's staging/merge-commit-marker logic, media files, or OS-crash conditions (only clean close without commit).
